candidates.title: Give "a note's path changed" one owning module
candidates.problem: Four modules each re-assemble their own partial version of the "a note moved from A to B" fanout, so every path-keyed consumer that one of them forgets goes stale with no single place to notice.
candidates.solution: Extract one module that owns a path change end-to-end -- `applyPathChange(oldPath, newPath | null)` as the sibling of `notifyAfterSave` -- and have `renameItem`, `moveItem`, `deleteItem` and `restoreItem` each end with exactly one call into it.
wins: One module owns note path changes
Folder-prefix remapping implemented once, not twice
Ordering contract stated once, not four times
Tests hit one interface, real stores
Caller interface shrinks to one call
candidates.deletionTest: Deleting the four inline assemblies concentrates complexity: today `renameItem` (fs.service.ts:201-244), `moveItem` (:247-284), `deleteItem` (:161-198) and `restoreItem` (trash.service.ts:101-146) each hand-pick a different subset of ten fanout steps, and the callers -- FileTreeItem.svelte:122 and :201, FileExplorer.svelte:194 and :253, TypeNoteList.svelte:291/325/351, auto-move.service.ts:183, type-definitions.service.ts:100, TrashSection.svelte:26 -- have no way to know which subset they got. After the merge each of the four keeps only its own precondition + disk operation and ends with one call; the fanout, the ordering contract, and the folder-prefix case exist exactly once. This is not hypothetical shape: `notifyAfterSave` (editor.hooks.ts:154-203) is already exactly this module for the sibling event "content changed at P", and nothing downstream re-assembles that fanout.

candidates.adrConflict: ADR-0003 line 50 (core/ may import only utils/) - but worth reopening because fs.service.ts:9 and editor.hooks.ts:3-8 already invert it today, and the observer-registry variant of this proposal (an addPathChangeObserver sibling to addAfterSaveObserver at editor.hooks.ts:109-117) would let bookmarks, collection, file-icons and calendar register themselves, removing the inversion instead of deepening it.
candidates.beforeShape: Six caller boxes (FileTreeItem.svelte, FileExplorer.svelte, TypeNoteList.svelte, auto-move.service.ts, type-definitions.service.ts, TrashSection.svelte) point at four assembly boxes: fs.service.renameItem, fs.service.moveItem, fs.service.deleteItem, trash.service.restoreItem. Each assembly box then draws its own arrow set into a shared pool of ten targets: plugin-fs.rename, link-updater.updateTabAfterRenameOrMove, link-updater.updateLinksAfterRename, fs.service.refreshTree, invoke('remove_note_from_index'), bookmarks.service.updateBookmarkPathsAfterMove, quickSwitcherStore.removeRecentPath, index-dedupe.clearIndexedEntry, editor.service.closeTabsForDeletedPath, trash.service.moveToTrash. renameItem draws six arrows, moveItem five, deleteItem six (three of them different ones), restoreItem exactly one (refreshTree). Three further path-keyed boxes sit in the diagram with zero inbound arrows from any of the four: collection.service.removeNoteFromIndex, fileIconsStore.frontmatterIcons, calendar.service's fileDateKeys/fileFrontmatterKeys maps.
candidates.afterShape: One new box, core/filesystem/path-change.service.ts, exporting applyPathChange(oldPath, newPath | null). renameItem, moveItem, deleteItem and restoreItem shrink to [precondition + disk op] with a single arrow into it. Every arrow from the before-diagram's pool moves inside that box, plus the three orphaned targets get wired in for the first time, and the folder-prefix walk (currently only in updateTabAfterRenameOrMove and bookmarks.logic) is implemented once there and applied to every consumer -- including a per-descendant invoke('remove_note_from_index') / invoke('update_note_in_index') pair, which is what makes a folder rename repair the Rust VaultIndex at all. Optionally the fanout targets become registered observers (addPathChangeObserver in editor.hooks.ts) so the arrows point outward-in and core/ stops importing features/.
candidates.testImpact: Today: fs.service.test.ts (923 lines) and fs.service.race-audit.test.ts (178 lines) both mock link-updater, bookmarks, editor.service and index-dedupe (fs.service.test.ts:25-53), so every fanout and ordering assertion is toHaveBeenCalledWith or a callOrder array on spies -- tests reaching past the interface, which is what ADR-0007 forbids. trash.service.test.ts (405 lines) is genuinely good: it uses the real trashStore and real trash.logic and covers restore-collision suffixes, orphan-container cleanup, and the manifest-write-failure path -- so trash/restore does have a test surface; what it cannot cover is the index fanout, because restoreItem has none. Untestable through today's interfaces: "after renaming folder /vault/Projects to /vault/Archive, no store and no Rust index key still holds a path under the old prefix" -- there is no single call to assert against, and the assertion would have to be duplicated across five separately-mocked modules. After: one applyPathChange call with real fsStore, editorStore, collectionStore, fileIconsStore, bookmarksStore and quickSwitcherStore, mocking only Tauri IPC and plugin-fs, asserting on real store state -- and the race-audit file collapses into ordering tests on that one interface.

candidates.title: Collapse the two note-creation modules into one
candidates.problem: Two modules both own "create a note and make the app consistent", and the one with nine callers omits the index update that the other one's code comment explains at length is mandatory.
candidates.solution: Make note-creator the single owner of note creation -- uniquify, parent dir, template, create_note, and the full new-file fanout behind one interface with an openInEditor option -- and delete fs.service.createFile in favour of it.
wins: One module owns note creation
New-note index fanout stated once
Caller interface shrinks to one call
Tests hit one interface
candidates.deletionTest: Deleting fs.service.createFile concentrates complexity rather than moving it: its nine callers -- FileExplorer.svelte:96, QuickSwitcher.svelte:44, MarkdownEditor.svelte:118, command-palette.service.ts:71, canvas.service.ts:12, kanban.service.ts:17, collection.service.ts:22, type-definitions.service.ts:68 and :132 -- each shrink to one call with options, and the create-time fanout (markRecentSave, create_note, per-file TS index updaters, refreshTree) is stated once instead of twice-and-a-half. The counter-case is real and should be checked first: four of those nine create non-markdown files (.canvas, .kanban, .collection, .view) that legitimately need no property-index update, so the merged module must branch on extension internally -- which is precisely the branch that today is decided by which of the two creators a caller happened to import.

candidates.title: Collapse the eleven copied block-decorator bodies into one defineBlockDecorator module

Interface shrinks to name plus compute

candidates.beforeShape: live-preview.ts imperatively pushes ~15 independently declared decorator constants, 6 of them behind an ad-hoc `isDisabled('name')` string check. Each of the 11 block files holds two masses: an exported pure `compute*(state) -> DecorationSet`, and a hand-copied `ViewPlugin.fromClass` body containing `decorations` + `lastCursorLine` fields, a constructor, the dead `viewportChanged` guard, a `checkUpdateAction(update, lastCursorLine)` gate, and `profileStart/profileEnd` with a per-file literal label. Three unsynchronised name tables exist for the same features: the exported identifiers (`codeBlockField`), the `isDisabled` strings in live-preview.ts:54-66 (`codeBlock`), and `DECORATOR_NAMES` in TroubleshootingSection.svelte:13-17. Two decorators carry real variation inside the copied body: callout-field.ts:258-264 rebuilds on `toggleCalloutFold`, queryjs-block-field.ts:78-81 lets `forceDecorationRebuild` through a stricter gate.
candidates.afterShape: A new `core/block-decorator.ts` exports `defineBlockDecorator({ name, compute, rebuildOn? }) -> Extension` holding the single copy of the update discipline (drag skip, same-line cursor no-op, forceDecorationRebuild pass-through, profiling label derived from `name`). A new `core/decorator-registry.ts` holds one array of `{ name, compute }` entries. live-preview.ts maps over that array applying `isDisabled(name)` uniformly to every decorator instead of six; TroubleshootingSection.svelte imports the same array for its toggle list, so the third name table disappears. Each of the 11 plugin files shrinks to its `compute*` function plus one `defineBlockDecorator` call. The two genuine variations become declared arguments — callout passes `rebuildOn: [toggleCalloutFold]`, queryjs passes `rebuildOn: [forceDecorationRebuild]` — so two real adapters exist for that parameter rather than one hypothetical one.
candidates.testImpact: Today 15 of the 16 files in src/tests/.../live-preview/plugins/ import only the exported `compute*`/`build*` function and build an `EditorState`; `grep -c 'new EditorView'` returns 0 for all but queryjs-block-field.test.ts. The update discipline — mouse-drag skip via `mouseSelectingField`, the same-line cursor no-op, forceDecorationRebuild pass-through, viewport-only skip — is therefore exercised once in the entire block track, and is untestable per plugin without duplicating the ~25 lines of jsdom EditorView scaffolding at queryjs-block-field.test.ts:16-38 into fifteen files. `core/check-update-action.test.ts` only feeds a hand-built fake ViewUpdate object, so it never proves a real plugin consumes the verdict correctly. After: one `block-decorator.test.ts` mounts a real EditorView with a stub `compute` that counts invocations and asserts all four gates once — the same harness pattern `inline-formatting-plugin.test.ts:27` already uses for stub handlers. Per-feature tests keep asserting on `compute*` output unchanged. A registry test becomes possible that asserts every registered decorator name appears in the settings toggle list, which would fail today on 6 inert names and 9 missing ones.

candidates.title: Fold the four surviving inline ViewPlugins into the inline handler registry
candidates.problem: Four inline decorators still walk the visible ranges themselves, re-deriving block-context skip and cursor reveal that `buildInlineDecorations` already derives on the same ranges in the same rebuild.
candidates.solution: Move them into `PRODUCTION_NODE_HANDLERS` / `PRODUCTION_LINE_HANDLERS`, adding the one thing NodeHandler lacks: a way to say "do not descend into my children".
wins: One tree walk, not five
Four ViewPlugin bodies deleted entirely
Cursor-reveal and block-context skip stop duplicating
Overlapping decorations become one testable set
candidates.deletionTest: Delete image-plugin.ts, footnote-plugin.ts, wikilink-embed-plugin.ts and meta-bind-input-plugin.ts as modules and their behaviour does not vanish — it reappears as four entries in the handler registry, one file each, minus four ViewPlugin bodies and four range walks. The complexity that concentrates is the walk itself: `buildInlineDecorations` already iterates the syntax tree and then the lines of the same expanded ranges, so the four callers are paying for a traversal that exists. Nothing is left behind except the parsers, which are already separate modules.

candidates.beforeShape: live-preview.ts:64-66 pushes `inlineExtensions()` and then, side by side, `imagePlugin`, `footnotePlugin`, `wikilinkEmbedPlugin` and (behind `isDisabled('metaBindInput')`) `metaBindInputPlugin`. Per rebuild the expanded visible ranges are traversed five times: `buildInlineDecorations` does one `syntaxTree.iterate` plus one per-line loop with `resolveInner`; imagePlugin does its own `syntaxTree.iterate`; footnotePlugin, wikilinkEmbedPlugin and metaBindInputPlugin each do their own per-line `resolveInner` loop. Each of the four re-implements the same two guards — `isInsideBlockContext(nodeAt)` and `shouldShowSource(...)` — and each produces its own DecorationSet that only meets the inline pipeline's set at the CodeMirror view layer.
candidates.afterShape: `imageHandler: NodeHandler { nodeType: 'Image' }` joins `PRODUCTION_NODE_HANDLERS`; `footnoteHandler`, `wikilinkEmbedHandler` and `metaBindInputHandler` join `PRODUCTION_LINE_HANDLERS` in inline-extensions.ts:25-47. `NodeHandler.decorate` gains a `false` return meaning "skip children" (image needs it, the mark handlers must not have it — two real adapters). `metaBindInputHandler` memoises its frontmatter parse in the existing `scratch: Map<string, unknown>` (inline-formatting-plugin.ts:26) instead of calling `state.doc.toString()` per rebuild. `inlineExtensions()` takes the disabled-decorator set so `metaBindInput` keeps its toggle by filtering the handler array. live-preview.ts:64-66 collapses to a single `exts.push(...inlineExtensions())`, and the four plugin files reduce to handler modules under `inline/handlers/`.

candidates.title: Give the five widget render caches one registered discipline
candidates.problem: Five widget caches are five hand-rolled Maps with five bespoke clear functions wired into vault teardown by hand, and the doc comments explaining which is which have already gone stale.
candidates.solution: One `createWidgetRenderCache<T>(name)` that self-registers, plus `clearAllWidgetCaches()` called once at teardown; queryjs keeps its live-DOM store but registers its reset.
wins: One cache discipline, not five
Teardown registration enforced, not remembered
Live-element invariant stated once
Tests hit one cache interface
candidates.deletionTest: Delete the shared cache module and each widget re-declares its own `Map`, its own exported `clear*Cache()`, and app-lifecycle.service.ts re-grows five imports and five call lines — precisely the shape that exists today at app-lifecycle.service.ts:73-76 and :411-415. The complexity that concentrates is not the Map, it is the contract: 'every widget cache must be dropped on vault teardown' and 'a cache must never hand the same live element to two widgets' are currently enforced by five hand-written call sites and three near-identical prose comments, with nothing that fails when a sixth cached widget forgets to register.

candidates.beforeShape: Five independent caches with no shared interface: `mathCache` (block-math-widget.ts:10), `inlineMathCache` (inline-math-widget.ts:10) and `mermaidCache` (mermaid-widget.ts:36) each store sanitized markup strings; `collectionCache` (collection-block-widget.ts:36) stores a `{ view, result }` data entry keyed `${yamlContent}|${indexSize}`; `queryjsSessionStore` stores live HTMLElements. Each exports its own `clear*Cache()`. app-lifecycle.service.ts imports four of them at :73-76 and calls all five at :411-415, next to `queryjsSessionStore.reset()`. Which widget uses which discipline is documented only in CLAUDE.md prose (Performance rule 2) and in per-file comments that already disagree with the code.
candidates.afterShape: A `widgets/render-cache.ts` exports `createWidgetRenderCache<T>(name): { get, set, clear }` which pushes itself into a module-level registry, and `clearAllWidgetCaches()`. block-math, inline-math and mermaid instantiate `createWidgetRenderCache<string>('block-math' | 'inline-math' | 'mermaid')`; collection instantiates `createWidgetRenderCache<CollectionCacheEntry>('collection')` — two real value shapes, so the generic is earned rather than speculative. queryjs keeps `queryjs-session.store.svelte.ts` intact (its live-DOM semantics and autoRun markers are governed by ADR-0010) and only registers its `reset` with the same registry. app-lifecycle.service.ts:411-415 becomes one `clearAllWidgetCaches()` call and one import. The five bespoke `clear*Cache` exports disappear from the widget modules' interfaces.
candidates.testImpact: Today each cache is tested only through its own clear function inside its own widget test (block-math-widget.test.ts:67, mermaid-widget.test.ts:35, collection-block-widget.test.ts:137). What no test covers, and what cannot be covered through the current interface, is the teardown contract itself: app-lifecycle.service.ts:411-415 is the only place the five caches are known to be a set, and asserting 'vault teardown drops every widget cache' would require a test to enumerate them by hand — reproducing the very list that can go stale. verdicts.title: Give "a note's path changed" one owning module
verdicts.reason:

So `remove_note_from_index` with a renamed folder's path is a no-op for every descendant. And watcher-handler.service.ts:38-49 drops directory-only batches (`basename.includes('.')` filter → `filePaths.length === 0` → return). refreshTree calls `scan_vault`, not `scan_vault_v2`, so it does not rebuild VaultIndex. "have renameItem, moveItem, deleteItem and restoreItem each end with exactly one call into it" contradicts commit 7070e56 ("fix(fs): prevent auto-save race on delete/rename/move"), which requires `closeTabsForDeletedPath` to run BEFORE the disk op in deleteItem (fs.service.ts:163-166). A single trailing call reintroduces the race the candidate's own cited race-audit file exists to pin. The module has to take the disk operation as a parameter (or expose a before/after pair), which enlarges the interface the proposal claims shrinks.
2. The signature `applyPathChange(oldPath, newPath | null)` cannot express restore (path appeared, no old path) or creation. That boundary is exactly candidate 2's territory, and neither candidate owns it.

For a renamed/moved/restored .md file the Rust watcher does repair Rust VaultIndex, file-icons, calendar, FTS and semantic via watcher-handler.service.ts:124-149; the residual TS gap is the un-removed old key in collectionStore.propertyIndex. verdicts.title: Collapse the two note-creation modules into one
verdicts.reason:
REFUTED as framed and as proposed, though it stumbled onto a real defect by accident.

The causal claim does not hold. note-creator.service.ts:86-94's comment explains that `kb.current()` returns null for first-open auto-run queryjs blocks unless `updateNoteInIndex` runs synchronously after `create_note`. But fs.service.ts:129 calls `invoke('create_note', { path: filePath, content: '' })` — createFile always creates an EMPTY file. An empty file contains no queryjs block, so the failure mode the comment describes cannot be reached through createFile. "MarkdownEditor.svelte:118 ... lands in exactly the state that comment describes as broken" is false.

The caller counts are wrong in both directions (see corrections), so the "nine vs five" framing that motivates the merge is not the real shape.

The proposed solution fits the wrong shape. createFile's contract is "create a new file in folder F with a collision-free name" (readDir + generateUniqueName, fs.service.ts:121-124). openOrCreateNote's contract is "open the note at exact path P, creating it from a template if absent, then focus it" (note-creator.service.ts:52-105). Merging them yields `createNote(options)` carrying mutually-exclusive mode flags — parentPath XOR filePath, uniquify, openInEditor, content XOR templatePath XOR inlineTemplate — over a ~60-line implementation. That is interface complexity approaching implementation complexity: a shallow module with an options bag, not a deepening. The candidate's own deletionTest already concedes the merged module "must branch on extension internally", which is a second mode flag.

The real defect, which the candidate walked past: createFile hardcodes `content: ''` and then calls `markRecentSave(filePath)` (fs.service.ts:129-130). Five callers immediately write real content afterwards — canvas.service.ts:12-15, kanban.service.ts:17-20, collection.service.ts:22-24, type-definitions.service.ts:68-70 and :132-137 — and because markRecentSave already flipped the self-save guard, watcher-handler.service.ts:46 skips the batch, so both the Rust VaultIndex and collectionStore.propertyIndex keep the EMPTY version until a full rescan. This is documented in-repo at type-definitions.service.ts:71-75 ("createFile's Rust create_note indexed the file EMPTY ... re-index explicitly or the new type only shows after a full vault rescan"), where exactly one of the five callers works around it with an explicit `invoke('update_note_in_index')`. canvas.service.ts:14 carries the same observation as a comment with no workaround.

The cheap deepening for that is to give createFile a `content` argument so the disk write and the index update happen once, in one place — not to delete it into a 17-caller options bag. That is a different proposal from the one on the table, so this candidate does not survive.

Not already done or planned: no task file or commit proposes either version.
evidenceCorrections: "nine callers" of createFile — there are ten production call sites. The list omits src/lib/core/markdown-editor/extensions/live-preview/wikilink-navigation.ts:42, which is a second unresolved-wikilink create path alongside MarkdownEditor.svelte:118.

"one of five plugin callers of openOrCreateNote (also templates.service.ts:62, note-composer.service.ts:43, one-on-one.service.ts:82, deep-link.service.ts:289)" — there are seven call sites. Missing: src/lib/features/type-definitions/type-definitions.service.ts:56 and src/lib/core/markdown-editor/extensions/live-preview/widgets/meta-bind-button-widget.ts:137.

So the before-shape has five create paths, not three.

verdicts.title: Make persistence a property of the settings module, not a duty of every mutation site
verdicts.reason:
Verified nearly end to end, and the code is worse than the candidate claims. Counts are exact: `rg -c "onchange\(\)"` returns 58 calls across 17 .svelte files, and there are exactly 14 `saveSettings(...)` call sites outside settings.service.ts (layout.service.ts:16, SettingsPanel.svelte:72, AppShell.svelte:69, update-check.service.ts:67, SidebarModeToggle.svelte:14, command-palette.service.ts:165/183/193, global-keybindings.ts:111/120, TagsPanel.svelte:23, TagsView.svelte:22, app-lifecycle.service.ts:297/312) spread over 9 modules. Every cited line says what is claimed: SettingsPanel.svelte:69-74 is the 500 ms debouncedSave handed down as `onchange`; EditorSection.svelte:99-107 is the oninput/onblur `updateEditor(...); onchange();` pair; TypesSection.svelte:19-22 is the setter-bypassing `setSettings({...settingsStore.settings, explicitOrganization: v}); onchange();`; layout.service.ts:12-18 and SidebarModeToggle.svelte:12-15 are two subtly different sidebarMode mutations (layout.service adds `leftSidebarVisible: true`, SidebarModeToggle does not) each carrying its own save; AppShell.svelte:67-73 is a second 300 ms debounced whole-store writer, and TagsPanel.svelte:21-27 / TagsView.svelte:20-26 are a third and fourth at 300 ms, so the 'four debounce policies' win is literally true.

The decisive fact the candidate MISSED, which strengthens it: two mutation sites have already forgotten step two. AppShell.svelte:102 and :109 call `settingsStore.updateLayout({leftSidebarVisible: !v})` / `{rightSidebarVisible: !v}` with NO saveSettings, while the identical toggles at global-keybindings.ts:109-111 / 118-120 and command-palette.service.ts:163-165 / 181-183 do persist. So toggling a sidebar with the button is forgotten across restarts and toggling it with Cmd+B is not. That is exactly the silent-regression class the two-step contract predicts, present in main today.

Deletion test re-run: deleting the `onchange` prop and the 13 non-panel `saveSettings` imports pushes nothing back onto callers — every one of those sites reduces to a bare `settingsStore.updateX(...)`. Complexity concentrates into one effect. The store setters survive the same test in the opposite direction (deleting them spreads spread-merge logic across 92 mutation sites), so they earn their keep. Technically feasible: every setter in settings.store.svelte.ts:165-360 reassigns the top-level `settings = {...}` signal, so a single `$effect` reading `settingsStore.settings` fires on all 92 sites, and AppShell is unconditionally mounted at (app)/+layout.svelte:190. ADR-0006 is satisfied, not violated — the effect reads the dependency then calls the service under `untrack()`, the canonical pattern. Nothing in tasks/todo/ or tasks/done/ proposes this.

What the candidate under-costs (does not refute, but the plan is bigger than 'a loading guard'): (a) app-lifecycle.service.ts:421 calls `resetSettings()` during vault teardown, which under the new scheme would schedule a write of DEFAULT_SETTINGS — the suppression must cover teardown, not just load; (b) the effect's initial run happens over the not-yet-hydrated DEFAULT_SETTINGS, so it needs a 'hydrated' gate or it can clobber settings.json in the window before loadSettings resolves; (c) app-lifecycle.service.ts:297/312 currently `await saveSettings(...)` before showing a toast, which becomes fire-and-forget. All three are internal to the settings module rather than caller duties, so the depth win holds.

TypesSection covers explicitOrganization (:20), showUntypedNotes (:35) and typesBaseFolder (:50-52); dockBadgeInboxCount's setter-bypassing setSettings call is in QuickCaptureSection.svelte:97.

verdicts.title: Fold defaults, the load-time merge, and the clamps into one settings schema
verdicts.reason:
Survives only in its second half, and the stated problem is partly wrong.

What checks out: settings.service.ts:54-164 really is a hand-expanded per-group merge; settings.store.svelte.ts:7-129 really is the same tree with values; settings.logic.ts:4-37 really holds seven clamp* functions whose ONLY callers are onblur handlers in EditorSection.svelte:104/127/150/173 and HeadingTypographyEditor.svelte:62/75/100; settings.service.ts imports only normalizeAppearance and headingTypographyToCssVars (lines 4-5), so `appearance` (theme.logic.ts:434-452) is the only validated group on the load path. A settings.json with `editor.fontSize: 400` or `null` is spread straight through at settings.service.ts:92-93 into settings.store, and MarkdownEditor.svelte:447-453 hands it to editor-theme.ts:26 as `${fontSize}px`. The oninput/onblur split at EditorSection.svelte:99-107 is a real user-reachable bug: clearing the number field yields `Number('') === 0`, the store takes 0, and the 500 ms debounce can write 0 to disk before blur ever fires (Escape unmounts the panel via SettingsPanel.svelte:89, and onDestroy flushes the debounce). settings.service.test.ts (706 lines, describes at 24/395/465/543/608/692) is exactly the hand-written per-group merge test the candidate describes, and settings.store.test.ts:105-140 does assert object spread one setter at a time.

What refutes the first half: the three declarations CANNOT silently drift. `DEFAULT_SETTINGS: AppSettings` (settings.store.svelte.ts:7) and `const merged: AppSettings = {...}` (settings.service.ts:54) are both compile-checked object literals against settings.types.ts, so adding a field to AppSettings is a `pnpm check` error at both other sites — that is the exhaustiveness guard the sync-settings commit relied on. Replacing the literal with a generic recursive merge necessarily returns `as AppSettings` and DELETES that guard, so the deletion test's 'complexity concentrates' conclusion is incomplete: a compile-time check moves from the type system to nothing. The cost of the 110 lines is verbosity, not correctness.

What refutes half the remedy: 'run one normalizeSettings() ... on the store's write path so disk-entered and UI-entered values pass the same guard' would break the number inputs. EditorSection binds `value={String(settingsStore.editor.fontSize)}`, so clamping on every store write means typing '1' on the way to '18' instantly rewrites the field to '8'. That is precisely why the clamp is onblur-only today — the proposal re-creates the bug the current shape avoids.

Surviving core: normalization belongs on the LOAD path (a `normalizeSettings` applied in loadSettings alongside normalizeAppearance) and on the COMMIT path (blur/commit, or clamp-before-persist inside the persistence owner from candidate 1), not on every keystroke. That is a genuine depth win — validity becomes an invariant of the settings module rather than a duty of two .svelte onblur handlers — and it is testable against merged store state today. Not already done, not in tasks/todo/ or tasks/done/, no ADR conflict (calling a .logic.ts from a store is explicitly allowed by ADR-0004).
evidenceCorrections: 'settings.types.ts:63 with settings.store.svelte.ts:59 and settings.service.ts:78-81 — layout.tagsVisible is declared, defaulted and merged in all three modules' — wrong on mechanism. settings.service.ts:78-81 spread-merges the whole `layout` group (`...DEFAULT_SETTINGS.layout, ...parsed.layout`); tagsVisible is never named there. verdicts.title: Collapse the four settings-section declarations into one registry
verdicts.reason:
Every citation is real and accurate. settings.types.ts:290 is the 17-member `SettingsSection` union; settings.logic.ts:61-104 is SETTINGS_SECTION_GROUPS (5 groups, 17 ids); SettingsPanel.svelte:49-67 is `sectionIcons: Record<SettingsSection, Component>`, which IS the only exhaustiveness-checked declaration since `Record<union, X>` demands every key while `readonly SettingsSectionGroup[]` demands nothing; SettingsPanel.svelte:130-164 is the 17-branch if/else, and a missing branch renders an empty `<div class="max-w-3xl px-10 py-8">` with a green `pnpm check`. theme-editor.logic.test.ts:199-227 does assert 51/19/51/5/6 token coverage per group, and settings.logic.test.ts:204-207 / 218-224 are exactly the hard-coded id list and the flat-list mirror.

The friction is empirically real, which the candidate did not prove but the history does: commit 4e6a1cc 'feat(sync): add Sync settings section and lifecycle wiring' touched settings.types.ts:308 (union), settings.logic.ts:91-97 (group), SettingsPanel.svelte:28,46,69,159-160 (import, icon import, icon map entry, if/else branch) and settings.logic.test.ts:206,217-220 — and its own message records the author hand-managing the lockstep: 'the SettingsSection union entry (deliberately deferred from Task 9 so the union and the panel's icon Record change together in one commit)'. But the framing is wrong and the payoff is smaller than the sibling candidates'. A registry array of 17 five-field entries has no behaviour behind it, so this is a single-source-of-truth / locality win, not a depth win — there is no interface leverage to gain, only drift to eliminate. Blast radius is correspondingly tiny: `SettingsSection` has only two consumers outside SettingsPanel.svelte (settings-panel.store.svelte.ts:1,4,11,17), so the 'four modules in lockstep' is really four declarations inside two files plus one type alias. The ADR-0004 note is honest and the relocation works, but it under-states one consequence: deriving `SettingsSection = typeof SETTINGS_SECTIONS[number]['id']` moves the canonical union out of settings.types.ts into a module that imports .svelte files. Type-only imports erase at build so settings-panel.store.svelte.ts stays clean at runtime, but settings.types.ts either loses ownership of the union or has to import it back from a framework-touching module.
evidenceCorrections: The proposed name `SETTINGS_SECTIONS` is already taken: settings.logic.ts:107 exports `SETTINGS_SECTIONS` as the flat list derived from SETTINGS_SECTION_GROUPS, and settings.logic.test.ts:218-224 tests it. The afterShape describes creating that identifier as if it were new.

'Adding one settings section means editing four modules in lockstep' — it is four declarations across three files (settings.types.ts, settings.logic.ts, SettingsPanel.svelte, the latter holding two of the four), not four modules.

It omits the second consequence: deriving the union from that registry relocates `SettingsSection` out of settings.types.ts into a module with .svelte imports, which settings-panel.store.svelte.ts:1 then imports from.

verdicts.title: Collapse the external-note-write protocol into one module
verdicts.reason:
The observation that external writers diverge is real, but the candidate's inventory is wrong in both directions and the proposed hub is refuted by what notifyAfterSave actually means.

(a) Two of the eight claimed "writers" do not write. src/lib/features/properties/properties.service.ts:39-50 (commitChanges) and src/lib/features/properties/lifecycle.service.ts:12-20 (commitLifecycleChange) contain no writeTextFile and no invoke — they mutate the tab and let auto-save do the disk write. They are not partial re-implementations of a write protocol; they are a different operation. The deletionTest's "eight partial re-implementations" is therefore inflated.

(b) Three real writers were missed entirely. src/lib/features/file-icons/frontmatter-icon.service.ts:46, :58, :75 rewrite a note's frontmatter bytes with ZERO of the four steps — no markRecentSave, no syncExternalContentToEditor, no index update. Setting an icon on an open note leaves the tab holding stale content, and the next auto-save clobbers the icon. The candidate never enumerated these, which means the "six subsets across eight sites" figure is not the result of an actual census.

(c) The fatal problem for the proposed hub: notifyAfterSave is not a neutral post-write fan-out. Its observer list (src/lib/core/editor/editor.hooks.ts:196-202) carries user-save semantics — src/lib/features/file-history/file-history.service.ts:192 snapshots the file, src/lib/features/auto-move/auto-move.service.ts:94-124 can physically relocate the note, src/lib/features/search/search.service.ts:311 updates FTS + semantic. Routing link-updater's rename propagation through it would create N file-history snapshots and N auto-move evaluations for one rename; routing tasks.service.ts:109 (a checkbox click) through it would snapshot on every toggle. The subsets differ because the semantics differ.

(d) The markRecentSave omission the candidate calls a defect is load-bearing. markRecentSave suppresses the watcher (watcher-handler.service.ts:46), and the watcher's incremental path (watcher-handler.service.ts:128-148) is the ONLY thing that gives link-updater's renamed files their collection / icon / calendar / FTS / semantic updates — link-updater itself only calls invoke('update_note_in_index'). Adding markRecentSave without also adding notifyAfterSave would silently stale FTS for every renamed file. So the hub is forced to choose between spurious snapshots/auto-moves and stale search, and the candidate never acknowledges the tension.

(e) Consequently the module cannot keep the promised "path plus content" interface. It needs flags for markRecentSave, markSaved, whether Rust already wrote, and whether this counts as a user save — an interface nearly as large as the implementation, i.e. a shallow module, which is the failure mode the review is supposed to avoid.

(f) An existing seam is ignored: addAfterSaveObserver already IS the extension point, with four real adapters (search, file-history, auto-move, SemanticIndexStatus). The candidate proposes a new hub without engaging with the one that exists.

What could survive is a narrower module — disk write + tab sync + Rust reindex, explicitly EXCLUDING the observer fan-out — covering link-updater.service.ts:38-50, type-definitions.service.ts:106-110 and :147-151, and the three unfixed frontmatter-icon sites. That is a different proposal from the one submitted, and it still has to answer (d).
evidenceCorrections: FALSE: 'src/lib/core/editor/editor.hooks.ts:193 — invalidateQueryjsCache() and clearLinkedContentCache() only ever run via notifyAfterSave'. Both also run at src/lib/core/app-lifecycle/watcher-handler.service.ts:82-83 (full rebuild) and :176-177 (incremental path). verdicts.title: Give the Rust VaultIndex one TypeScript reader
verdicts.reason:
SURVIVES ONLY IN HALF, AND THE WEAKER HALF IS THE HEADLINE. What checks out: three hand-rolled version-gate spellings genuinely exist (backlinks.service.ts:36-37 two Maps keyed on version; outgoing-links.service.ts:22 a composite `${version}:${contentLen}:${path}` key; completion.ts:28-30 a module-level cachedEntries/cachedVersion/pendingFetch), and outgoing-links.service.ts:10 literally says 'Same stale-tab guard as backlinks.service.ts::isStillCurrentPath'. Ten `get_all_vault_entries_v2` call sites are real (app-lifecycle.service.ts:213, graph-view.service.ts:15, type-definitions.service.ts:23, file-icons.service.ts:170, search.service.ts:32 and :51, completion.ts:38, lifecycle-filter.service.ts:8, tauri-listeners.service.ts:106, queryjs-block-widget.ts:184) and src-tauri/src/commands/vault.rs:478 does clone-then-sort every entry per call. A version-keyed memo behind an `entries()` interface is a real, small, deep win.

What does NOT survive:
(1) THE CENTRAL FRAMING IS A CATEGORY ERROR. 'Every reader of the Rust VaultIndex ... re-fetches its own copy of the full snapshot' is false. The version-gate owners (backlinks, outgoing, tags) read TARGETED commands — get_backlinks_v2, get_outgoing_links_v2, get_all_tags_v2 — and never touch the snapshot. The snapshot readers (graph-view, file-icons, search, queryjs, app-lifecycle) own no version gate. Only completion.ts and tauri-listeners.ts are in both sets. The candidate welds two unrelated problems into one module and calls the result one interface.
(2) THE BURST-COLLAPSE CONCERN IS ALREADY CENTRALIZED. tauri-listeners.service.ts:121 debounces `refresh` 300 ms, and :104 bumps the version INSIDE that debounce. The comment at :89-91 states it outright: 'Debouncing the bump itself also collapses the burst for every vaultIndexVersion consumer (TasksView, GraphView, panels)', and tauri-listeners.service.test.ts:502 asserts a three-event burst produces exactly one bump. So the candidate's claim that tasks.service.ts having no guard means 'a save burst re-runs the full task aggregation N times' is refuted by the code it cites two lines earlier. Same for graph-view. Two of the three 'concerns' (burst collapse, in-flight collapse) already live in shared modules — `debounce` at the bump and `dedupeInflight` at utils/inflight.ts:27.
(3) THE PROPOSED INTERFACE WOULD BE SHALLOW. `subscribe(fetch, apply)` cannot express the actual variation: backlinks keys on (path, version) with an active-path guard; outgoing adds content.length; tags is global with a 300 ms debounce and no version gate; tasks additionally depends on tasksStore.sectionTag, which is not the version at all (tasks.service.ts:81-84). Making one interface serve all of them requires keyFn + debounceMs + staleness-guard knobs — the interface would carry most of the implementation's complexity, which is the definition of shallow.
(4) THE SNAPSHOT MEMO HAS AN UNADDRESSED CORRECTNESS HAZARD. vaultStore.open() (vault.store.svelte.ts:51-58) does not reset vaultIndexVersion, and the counter lags Rust by the 300 ms debounce. A cache keyed on that counter would serve the PREVIOUS vault's entries after a vault switch, and would serve stale data to search.service.ts and app-lifecycle.service.ts:213, which today always get fresh reads.

Narrower and defensible restatement: memoize `get_all_vault_entries_v2` by version behind one `entries()` call (extending tasks/todo/audit-vault-and-freeze.md item 17 from queryjs-only to all snapshot readers), and unify the three version-gate spellings across backlinks/outgoing/completion. Leave the panel subscribe protocol alone.
evidenceCorrections: 'tasks/todo/audit-vault-and-freeze.md:17' — wrong location. Line 17 is Tier 1 item 4 (MAX_NOTE_SIZE on update_note_in_index). The queryjs memoization is ITEM 17, at line 39: '(optional) perf(queryjs): memoize get_all_vault_entries_v2 by vaultIndexVersion. NOT DONE'.

'tasks.service.ts:53 — buildTaskIndex re-invokes get_all_tasks_v2 unguarded, so a save burst re-runs the full task aggregation N times' — the consequence is false. The version bump is itself debounced 300 ms (tauri-listeners.service.ts:121, documented at :89-91, asserted by tauri-listeners.service.test.ts:502), so a burst produces ONE bump and therefore ONE buildTaskIndex. Also off by one: line 53 is a comment terminator; buildTaskIndex is at :54.

'tauri-listeners.service.ts:97 — a fifth spelling: 300 ms debounce + fetchSeq latest-wins, applied only to this one fan-out' — misleading. Only fetchSeq is fan-out-local. The 300 ms debounce is applied to the version bump itself and therefore governs every vaultIndexVersion consumer in the app.

'docs/adr/0025-rust-vault-index.md — the ADR asks for this module and it was never built' — misreading. The quoted sentence ('New consumers subscribe to vault-index-updated and read via get_*_v2 commands; they do not reimplement orchestration') is about not rebuilding TS-side metadata indexers, which is exactly what consumers do today. 'ten get_all_vault_entries_v2 call sites currently pay for [the snapshot] individually' per version — false in practice. Only tauri-listeners (:106) fires on every version bump; graph-view (:15) fires per bump only while GraphView is mounted; file-icons (:170) fires on vault open and full watcher rebuild (app-lifecycle.service.ts:253, watcher-handler.service.ts:75); search (:32/:51) documents itself as firing 'only on rare conditions'; app-lifecycle (:213) is one-shot; completion (:38) is already memoized by version. verdicts.title: Collapse note-write and index-notify into one module
verdicts.reason:
SURVIVES. Every load-bearing citation checked out, and the ADR violation is documented verbatim in the repo's own ADR.

VERIFIED: docs/adr/0009-incremental-indexing-reverse-index.md:63 reads 'Any function that mutates vault state (delete, rename, move) must call clearIndexedEntry(path) or risk stale dedupe skipping a re-creation.' fs.service.ts:184 calls it inside deleteItem; renameItem (:229) and moveItem (:269) call only invoke('remove_note_from_index') and never clearIndexedEntry. That is an active, uncontested ADR violation in two of the three named functions.

DELETION TEST HOLDS, AND THE CALLER COUNT IS REAL — I counted more sites than the candidate did. Markdown-note writes that skip some or all of the fan-out: frontmatter-icon.service.ts:46/:58/:75 (bare writeTextFile, no notify at all), file-icons.service.ts:97 (ensureFolderNote writes '---\n---\n', bare, uncited by the candidate), kanban.service.ts:20, collection.service.ts:24, type-definitions.service.ts:70+75 (write + reindex), :106-108 (write + sync + reindex, no markRecentSave), :136 (bare), :147-151 (write + sync(false) + reindex), link-updater.service.ts:38-49 (write + sync + reindex), note-creator.service.ts:81-95 (create_note + markRecentSave + TS mirror), deep-link.service.ts six sites, editor.service.ts:144-147 (write + notifyAfterSave). That is 15+ sites across at least five distinct subsets of one ordered protocol. Delete the proposed module and every one of those subsets reappears — which is literally today's state. Not a pass-through.

THE SEAM IS REAL, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: two adapters minimum on each side (writeNote has 15+, forgetNote has 3 — delete/rename/move — of which 2 are already wrong).

NOT SHIPPED, NOT PLANNED: nothing in tasks/todo, tasks/done, or the last 60 commits touches this. tasks/todo/performance-architecture-refactor.md:95 confirms the fan-out already went wrong once ('Added remove_note_from_index Rust command ... to fix the deletion leak in fs.service.ts').

NOT SHALLOW: writeNote(path, content) / forgetNote(path) is a two-function interface over an ordered five-step fan-out whose ordering is load-bearing (markRecentSave must precede the disk write or the watcher's areAllRecentSaves guard misses it — note-creator.service.ts:82-84 explains this in prose to every future writer). Small interface, real invariants behind it.

DOES NOT CONTRADICT AN ADR — it enforces ADR-0009. And syncExternalContentToEditor is already a no-op for unopened paths (editor.service.ts:37-38, `if (!tab) return`), so most of the 'different subsets' variation is spurious rather than semantic, which strengthens the merge.

CAVEATS THE PROPOSAL MUST HANDLE: (a) the bare-write sites are not simply broken — they currently rely on the Rust watcher to index them; routing them through writeNote's markRecentSave would SUPPRESS the watcher and make the explicit update_note_in_index load-bearing. That is a behaviour change, not a pure refactor, and needs the trace-before-remove ritual. (b) note-creator uses invoke('create_note') rather than writeTextFile and will not fit writeNote unchanged. (c) canvas/settings/trash/bookmarks/todoist/log writes must stay OUT — the caller still has to know which writes are notes.
evidenceCorrections: 'deep-link.service.ts:234 — the only SITE that runs all four steps in order' — wrong count. Four of deep-link's six write sites run all four: :234-237, :252-255, :268-271 and :330-333. Only :284-286 and :441-443 omit syncExternalContentToEditor. The accurate claim is 'the only SERVICE that runs all four steps'.
'editor.hooks.ts:182 — a 9-line comment' — the IMPORTANT paragraph is 7 lines (:182-188). Minor.

'index-updater.service.ts:40 — the same call sits INSIDE the same guard here; two callers, two placements of one call against one guard' — cited correctly (line 40 is the early return, the invoke at :48 is behind it), but framed as a defect when it is deliberate and safe: anything that set the dedupe signature also called Rust, so skipping Rust on a signature hit cannot lose an update. editor.hooks.ts:182-188 documents exactly why its own placement differs. Use it as evidence of scattered knowledge, not of a bug.

testImpact: 'The rename/move clearIndexedEntry gap is therefore untestable through the current interface' — false. index-dedupe.ts:19 exports isAlreadyIndexed, so a test could drop the vi.mock at fs.service.test.ts:40-42, call markIndexed(oldPath, content), run renameItem, and assert isAlreadyIndexed(oldPath, content) === false. The candidate omits frontmatter-icon.service.ts's actual failure mode. Those three bare writes are not silently unindexed — the Rust watcher (500 ms debounce, watcher-handler.service.ts:131-133) picks them up because no markRecentSave suppresses it. The defect is latency and inconsistency, not a lost index update. Stating it as 'no index update' overclaims.

Uncited supporting site the proposal should include: file-icons.service.ts:97 (ensureFolderNote) writes a markdown note with no markRecentSave, no update_note_in_index and no editor sync — a sixth subset.

verdicts.title: Make initializeVault own the whole vault-open sequence, including its deferred tail
verdicts.reason: Every code citation checks out. app-lifecycle.service.ts:228-234 does carry the comment saying autoOpenDailyNote is deliberately NOT called there; +layout.svelte:72-76 and :82-84 do append the two tail steps in the `.then`; app-lifecycle.service.ts:117-122 does saveAllDirtyTabs-then-teardownVault while +layout.svelte:91 calls teardownVault bare; the test at src/tests/lib/core/app-lifecycle/app-lifecycle.service.test.ts:227 is verbatim `expect(autoOpenDailyNote).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`. So the verification hole is real: nothing anywhere tests that opening a vault opens the daily note, that the update check runs after settings load, or that a vault switch saves dirty tabs first. I also found a defect the candidate did NOT claim, which strengthens it: initializeVault early-returns (and thus resolves) at :133, :160, :163, :192, :207 and :224, so the +layout `.then` tail fires autoOpenDailyNote and maybeAutoCheckForUpdates even when open_vault_db failed or a rapid vault switch invalidated the init. More seriously, the solution says to move 'the per-vault listener registrations' into app-lifecycle: those registrations are NOT per-vault. registerDeepLinkListener must be live BEFORE any vault is open — deep-link.service.ts:130-139 stores a pending action and calls vaultStore.open() precisely because the listener already caught a URL with no vault (or a different vault) open. Same for registerCloseHandler, registerMenuSettingsListener and registerQuickCaptureListener. Folding them into a vault-lifecycle module conflates app-mount scope with vault scope; at most they can be collapsed into one non-vault registration effect, which is cosmetic. Likewise the 'split feature' framing of executePendingAction (app-lifecycle:338) vs registerDeepLinkListener (+layout:40) is not a defect — the register/execute split across app-mount and vault-open is inherent to the feature. Finally, the close-path asymmetry is latent to the point of being unreachable: `rg` finds zero production callers of vault.service.ts:38 closeVault and zero other callers of vaultStore.close(), so the else-branch teardownVault at +layout:91 only fires at mount with no vault. Downgraded from Strong because the actionable payload is two fire-and-forget calls, not a nine-step sequence. Note also a naming collision: app-lifecycle exporting `closeVault` clashes with the existing export at src/lib/core/vault/vault.service.ts:38.
evidenceCorrections: beforeShape says +layout.svelte holds 'nine $effects'. It holds 11 (grep -c '$effect(' src/routes/(app)/+layout.svelte = 11): seven dep-less registrations (lines 27, 32, 36, 40, 44, 48, 52), the vault effect (57), and three data effects (110, 152, 175).
beforeShape says 'six dep-less registrations' and then lists seven names. There are seven.
The files list says the test file has '~30 vi.mock blocks'. rg -c '^vi\.mock' returns 26.

The solution's 'per-vault listener registrations' are not per-vault. registerDeepLinkListener, registerCloseHandler, registerMenuSettingsListener, registerQuickCaptureListener and registerFocusListener are app-mount scoped and must survive vault open/close — deep-link.service.ts:130-139 depends on the listener being live while a DIFFERENT vault (or none) is open. Moving them inside openVault would be a behavior regression.

Evidence item 6 frames executePendingAction (app-lifecycle:338) / registerDeepLinkListener (+layout:40) as 'splitting one feature across the seam'. The lines are correct but the split is inherent to the feature (register at app mount, execute at vault open), not an accident of the current shape.

verdicts.title: Give "a note's bytes changed" one module instead of four divergent fan-out lists

verdicts.reason:
Refuted as a deepening. Every citation is real — I opened all eight and they say what is claimed, including the stale comment at queryjs-block-widget.ts:95 (rg for `isConnected` across src/lib returns hits only in queryjs-block-widget.ts and an unrelated GraphView.svelte variable, so mermaid/collection/block-math provably have no such guard) and the untested teardown at app-lifecycle.service.ts:410-415 (teardownVault has ~15 tests in app-lifecycle.service.test.ts:396-560 and none references any clear function). The problems are real. The proposed module is not the fix.

The deletion test fails. Delete `createWidgetRenderCache` and what reappears is four `new Map<K,V>()` declarations and four one-line `clear*Cache()` exports — verified by rg: only inline-math-widget.ts:10, block-math-widget.ts:10, collection-block-widget.ts:36 and mermaid-widget.ts:36 are module-level widget caches. That is roughly sixteen trivial lines. `new Map()` is not complexity; nothing concentrates. Meanwhile the new module's interface (a name, a generic parameter T, get/set/clear, a module-level registry, plus `clearAllWidgetCaches`) is as large as its implementation — the textbook shallow module.

The seam is hypothetical where it matters. Four instantiations but only two value shapes, and the candidate's own afterShape deliberately keeps the ONE genuinely different discipline (queryjs's live-DOM store) OUT of the module. The interesting variation is excluded from the seam by construction, so the generic buys nothing beyond `Map<string, string>` vs `Map<string, CollectionCacheEntry>`.

The headline win is not delivered by the design. "Live-element invariant stated once" and "'stores a live element' becomes a property of the cache instance rather than a claim in a comment" are unsupported: nothing in `createWidgetRenderCache<T>(name)` prevents `T = HTMLElement`. The invariant stays prose, exactly as today in the three near-identical comments at block-math-widget.ts:5-9, inline-math-widget.ts:5-9 and mermaid-widget.ts:30-35.

The one real problem — teardown registration is remembered, not enforced, and untested — has a much smaller fix that does not touch any widget's interface: a `widgets/clear-caches.ts` exporting `clearAllWidgetCaches()` that calls the four existing exports, plus one test that asserts teardownVault empties all four. app-lifecycle.service.ts drops from four imports and four calls to one and one; no widget author has to learn a new cache interface. The stale comment at queryjs-block-widget.ts:95 is a one-line correction worth making on its own. Neither is an architecture finding.

No ADR conflict (the candidate's own ADR-0010 caveat is correctly reasoned), and no prior work: git log shows the four string/data caches were introduced together in de8a46f / f05100e / 8a6e855 / 65c8d0b, and no todo or done plan proposes unifying them.
evidenceCorrections: "Five widget caches are five hand-rolled Maps with five bespoke clear functions" is wrong on the count. There are FOUR module-level Maps with four `clear*Cache()` exports (inline-math-widget.ts:10, block-math-widget.ts:10, collection-block-widget.ts:36, mermaid-widget.ts:36). The fifth is `queryjsSessionStore`, a Svelte `$state` store with a `reset()` method, and its reset has a second call site outside teardown at QueryjsSection.svelte:42 — so "five bespoke clear functions wired into vault teardown by hand" describes four functions plus one store reset that is not teardown-only.
"mermaid-widget.test.ts:35" is a `clearMermaidCache()` call inside `beforeEach`, not a cache test. The actual cache test is `it('clearMermaidCache forces a new mermaid render')` at :87.
"collection-block-widget.test.ts:137" is likewise a `clearCollectionCache()` call inside `beforeEach`. The collection cache tests are the describe block at :116 and the assertions at :175 and :185.

Not a wrong citation but an unsupported inference: afterShape claims the generic is "earned rather than speculative" from two value shapes. Three of the four instantiations are `<string>`; the fourth is the only other shape, and the one cache with genuinely different semantics is excluded from the module.

verdicts.title: Give the property index one producer and one version
verdicts.reason: The thesis holds and I could reproduce the divergence end-to-end. collectionStore (collection.store.svelte.ts:9-38) really is fed by two producers writing the same Map: buildPropertyIndex via invoke('get_all_property_records') (collection.service.ts:65-79) and the TS buildNoteRecord path (collection.service.ts:93-103 -> collection.logic.ts:21-48). The shapes genuinely differ. src-tauri/src/commands/vault.rs:761-763 ALWAYS inserts bare `organized`/`archived`/`favorite`; the TS producer never does, because parseFrontmatterProperties canonicalizes those keys to `_organized`/`_archived`/`_favorite` (properties.logic.ts:146). The evaluator resolves a bare `organized` identifier straight out of record.properties with no alias (evaluator.ts:45-46, 91-93 aliases only `type`), so the filter exercised by portent-filters.test.ts:41-46 stops matching the moment any of the four TS call sites replaces the record. Same for relationship targets: vault.rs:768-775 emits extracted wikilink targets, the TS producer emits the raw frontmatter value. I confirmed removeNoteFromIndex (collection.service.ts:108-110) has ZERO call sites in src/lib -- the watcher delete branch (watcher-handler.service.ts:194-212) calls clearIndexedEntry + invoke('remove_note_from_index') and never touches the TS store, so deleted notes really do linger as phantom pages. The two ad-hoc freshness proxies are real and cited correctly (collection-block-widget.ts:52-53; queryjs-block-widget.ts:31-33 with its Phase-12.5 deletion note). Deletion test re-run: deleting the TS producer's write does concentrate, not move -- the four call sites (editor.hooks.ts:172, watcher-handler.service.ts:128, index-updater.service.ts:59, note-creator.service.ts:94) all already have a Rust round trip in flight, so none of them grows. Not already done and not planned: perf-architecture-refactor 8.5 migrated only buildPropertyIndex; updateNoteInIndex was deliberately KEPT as a documented TS fast path. Aligns with rather than contradicts ADR-0025, whose stated end state is 'zero TS metadata indexers'. Downgraded from Strong because four mechanical claims are wrong (see corrections), because the shim-deletion win is already scheduled under a different mechanism, and because the proposal does not address the sync->async semantics change: the TS producer is synchronous by design (note-creator.service.ts:83-93 documents that kb.current() returns null for auto-run queryjs blocks without it), and feeding the store from an IPC reply reorders it after notifyAfterSave's synchronous observer fan-out and invalidateQueryjsCache() at editor.hooks.ts:193.
evidenceCorrections: note-creator.service.ts:94 does NOT fire invoke('update_note_in_index'). It fires invoke('create_note') (note-creator.service.ts:81). create_note does update the index and return UpdateResult (src-tauri/src/commands/vault.rs:885-911), so the fix is analogous, but the claim 'the four TS callers each already fire invoke(update_note_in_index) in the same tick' is 3/4, and the proposal needs a second Rust command changed.

update_note_in_index does not return the projected record. It returns UpdateResult { changed, affected, version } (src-tauri/src/vault/index.rs:26-39). The solution's parenthetical '(returned by the update_note_in_index call the same paths already make)' describes an API that does not exist; the proposal requires adding the NoteRecord to UpdateResult (or a new command) on both update_note_in_index and create_note.

'the TS producer inserts none of these [_type, ...]' is wrong for _type. buildNoteRecord -> parseFrontmatterProperties -> canonicalizeKey maps bare `type:` to `_type` (properties.logic.ts:146), pinned by auto-move.logic.test.ts:266-273. And the collection evaluator aliases the bare `type` identifier to `_type` (evaluator.ts:91-93), so _type does not diverge in practice. The real divergences are the always-present bare organized/archived/favorite (vault.rs:761-763) and the extracted _belongs_to/_related_to/_has_many arrays (vault.rs:768-775).

beforeShape/afterShape undercount the readers. executeQuery has FOUR call sites in src/lib, not three: collection-block-widget.ts:91, CollectionView.svelte:175, TypeSidebar.svelte:103, TypeNoteList.svelte:221. The last two are omitted entirely from beforeShape.

The 'deletes the invalidateQueryjsCache shim' win is already planned, with a different mechanism: docs/adr/0010-queryjs-kb-api-caching.md:42 schedules narrowing notifyAfterSave to queryjsSessionStore.invalidate(jsContent) per just-edited block, not a version-keyed cache.

verdicts.title: Collapse the .collection YAML write paths into one patch
verdicts.reason: Citations are almost all accurate -- yaml-parser.ts:243-325 really is 83 lines of four mutators; updateCollectionYaml:172-229 really does apply seven optional view-field patches under one parse; CollectionView.svelte:39-50 is the 12-line latch comment; :195-198, :264-267 and :273-275 really are the same three-line latch block written out three times; the four mutators really have exactly ONE caller each (CollectionView.svelte:282, 291, 297, 318 -- verified by rg across src/). But the deletion test fails on re-run. Deleting the four mutators does not concentrate complexity, it moves it: each carries a DISTINCT invariant that must survive the merge (addView:251 initialises a missing views array and takes no index; removeView:274 refuses to drop the last view; renameView:286-287 trims and rejects empty names; setViewType has only the range guard). Folding them into updateCollectionYaml grows its patch type from 9 fields to 13 and introduces ordering semantics that do not exist today (does viewIndex apply before or after an addView in the same patch? after a removeViewAt?). That is a bigger interface behind the same behaviour -- the shallow-module failure mode the review is supposed to catch. Meanwhile the genuinely valuable half needs no yaml-parser change at all: commitStructural (CollectionView.svelte:271-276) ALREADY is the single-latch helper; persistState:195-198 and persistCalendarConfig:264-267 simply do not call it. Routing them through it is a three-line local edit, not an architecture finding, and it does not require touching the mutators. The KanbanView corroboration (KanbanView.svelte:64-83) shows the latch idiom recurs, but M27 is a bug in a module with a SINGLE write path, which is evidence that consolidating write paths would not have prevented it.
evidenceCorrections: tasks/todo/bug-hunt-fixes.md:44 is wrong for M27 -- M27 is at line 41 (line 44 is M19, the folder-notes _order bug). The entry itself cites KanbanView.svelte:64-82.

'src/tests/.../yaml-parser.test.ts:693-838 -- four describe blocks repeating the same happy / parse-failure / out-of-range trio' overstates. The four blocks do not repeat one trio: addView tests default type / requested type / missing-views-key init / parse failure; removeView tests remove / refuse-last-view / out-of-range / parse failure; renameView tests rename / trim / reject-empty / out-of-range; setViewType tests change / calendar-config preservation / out-of-range. Each block pins a different invariant.

testImpact claims the composite case 'rename a view and change its sort in one write' is 'unreachable because the two mutators each stringify independently'. False -- every mutator is string -> string, so updateCollectionYaml(renameView(yaml, i, name), { viewSort, viewIndex: i }) composes today and is directly testable. Only the number of parse/stringify round trips differs.
KanbanView.svelte latch spans 64-83 (comment 64, flag 65, effect 68-75, applyChange 78-83), cited as 63-82.

verdicts.title: Make the filter row/expression mapping one table
verdicts.reason: The BUG is real and I reproduced it by reading the code: parse("name > 'abc'") yields a binary node with a string right-hand side, parseBinaryToRow:330 calls mapBinaryOp(op, ast.right.type === 'number') = mapBinaryOp('>', false), the non-numeric branch at filter.logic.ts:439 returns 'gt', and the 'gt' emitter at :61 writes the value unquoted -> `name > abc`, where the literal becomes an identifier. Since CollectionView.svelte:165,184 feeds filterGroupsToFilter into the persisted YAML on any toolbar action, a hand-authored or Obsidian-authored `created > '2026-01-01'` is silently corrupted on disk. That is worth filing as a bug next to L34. But the candidate does NOT survive as an architecture finding. Its central evidentiary claim is false: the file is full of round-trip assertions. And the diagnosis 'no test CAN state the round-trip invariant because the two directions share no enumeration' does not hold -- FilterOperator is a closed union (toolbar.types.ts:2-27) that a test can enumerate exhaustively today via Record<FilterOperator, Case>, with no production change. The minimal fix is smaller still: drop the four relational cases from mapBinaryOp's non-numeric branch (:439-442) so astToFilterRow returns null and parseExpressionToRow:29 falls through to the `raw` passthrough, which filterRowToExpression:38 round-trips verbatim. Re-running the deletion test on the proposed OPERATOR_SPECS: the two directions are not symmetric. The emitter is a total per-operator function, but the matcher is an ORDERED cascade -- date-call before boolean before number before string (filter.logic.ts:309-330) -- so a table of per-operator matchers needs a new explicit precedence concept in its interface, and getOperatorsForType:172-185 would lose its deliberate menu ordering when derived from a `types` field. Complexity moves and grows rather than concentrating.
evidenceCorrections: 'grep finds no round-trip assertion anywhere in the file' is FALSE. src/tests/lib/features/collection/toolbar/filter-logic.test.ts contains at least seven explicit round-trip assertions: :253-262 (text equality), :264-272 (numeric comparison), :274-282 (contains), :283-292 (quote escaping), :310-317 (contains with quotes), :329-337 (numeric-looking text value), and :392-405 (groups -> filter -> groups).

FilterOperator has 20 members, not 21 (toolbar.types.ts:2-27: is, is_not, contains, does_not_contain, starts_with, ends_with, eq, neq, gt, lt, gte, lte, before, after, on_or_before, on_or_after, is_true, is_false, is_empty, is_not_empty). filterRowToExpression:43-84 has 20 cases accordingly.

The caller list is wrong in both directions. FilterPanel.svelte imports only createEmptyFilterRow and inferPropertyType (FilterPanel.svelte:19), never the mapping functions. And type-note-list.logic.ts:47-48, 79-82, 121-122 is an unlisted caller of parseFilterToGroups / filterGroupsToFilter, so 'nothing fans out' understates the blast radius of changing that interface.
